title: First 10 Days — Engineer Silent Launch Notes and Rapid Handoff Protocol
content:
Purpose: A compact, low-noise onboarding companion for engineers joining distributed teams. This is intentionally lightweight — focused on removing friction, reducing interrupt overhead during week 0–1, and creating a reproducible handoff that a pod can follow without a heavy orientation ceremony. Use this for hiring follow-ups, onboarding handoffs, and emergency backfills.

Who this is for: hiring manager, onboarding buddy, hiring coordinator, and the new hire (IC engineer). Use for individual ICs (infra, platform, runtime) but adaptable across eng groups.

High level goals (10-day sprint):
- Day 0–2: access + quiet signals (minimal required meetings, confirm infra access).
- Day 3–5: first small contributor cycle (tiny PR, pair-oncall doc, or low-risk infra change).
- Day 6–10: broaden context, 1:1s with key collaborators, handoff artifact creation.

Quick rules (silent launch philosophy):
- Default to asynchronous where possible (Slack + doc comments).
- Limit synchronous touchpoints to 30 minutes total across days 0–3 unless the new hire requests more.
- Provide clear micro-tasks (<= 4 hours) that ship something visible by day 5.
- Buddy should proactively unblock tooling but not drive the learning path end-to-end.

Day-by-day checklist (practical, prioritized):
Day 0 (pre-boarding):
- Send "Welcome packet" email with: Slack intro phrasing, calendar stub labeled "quiet-launch: optional orientation", hardware shipping tracking, and key Confluence links (access guide, infra runbook).
- Confirm account invites: Google, Okta, GitHub, PagerDuty, Slack. Capture any failures and escalate to infra-sre.

Day 1:
- Silent check-in: short Slack DM from buddy (template below).
- Confirm dev laptop booted, VPN works, repo clones.
- Assign micro-task #1: small repo read + open an issue or doc PR tagging mentor.
- Add new hire to minimal oncall rotation read list (no pages assigned).

Day 2:
- Verify CI access and ability to run local tests.
- Pair with buddy for 60 minutes max on the micro-task if requested.
- Hiring manager shares high-level objectives (3 bullet items) via doc — no synchronous meeting required.

Day 3:
- New hire opens a small PR or docs change; buddy reviews within 24 hours.
- Manager schedules 15-minute "alignment" async notes (bullet summary in Confluence).
- Set up 1:1 cadence (weekly 30m for first 8 weeks).

Day 4–5:
- Micro-task #2: deploy-test flow or follow a guided runbook.
- Shadow a short standup (watch only) and post one question to thread.
- Post a 3-line status update in the day-5 onboarding doc (what went well, blockers, first impact).

Day 6–7:
- First real review cycle: take ownership of a minor bug or doc section and work through PR feedback.
- Manager and buddy provide focused feedback (async comments preferred).
- Introduce to cross-functional partner(s) with an agenda in the invite (5 bullet agenda).

Day 8–10:
- Deliver a short artifact: either a small feature PR merged, a runbook improvement, or a performance test baseline.
- Handoff packet created by the new hire (see "Handoff packet" section).
- Team retrospective-lite: 20 minutes optional for feedback on the onboarding flow.

Handoff packet (artifact new hire produces by day 10):
- README-lite: what I worked on (3 bullets), how to run locally (2 commands), key TODOs.
- PR links and review notes.
- One-line risk signal: what still feels blocked or risky for the product area.

Interview/evaluator micro-rubric (for later calibration of hiring signal):
- Technical execution (0–4): Can the candidate convert a small spec into working code in <=2 hours?
- System thinking (0–4): Can they outline failure modes and simple mitigations?
- Communication (0–3): Can they explain tradeoffs and next steps clearly?
- Team fit (0–2): Pragmatic collaborator, asks clarifying questions, accepts feedback.
- Quick guidance: target score for hire=9+, for hire-with-coaching=7–8. Store rubrics in hiring folder and tag by role.

Hiring plan notes (compact):
- For early IC hires on infra/runtime teams prioritize: reproducible dev setup, infra access, and first deployable artifact by week 2.
- Reserve a small "onboarding project" seed in the roadmap (2–4 days of work) so hiring cycles don’t block sprint delivery.
- Budget note: include one-time allocation for hardware or VPN token provisioning in offer checklist.

Quiet-intro Slack DM template (buddy -> new hire):
- "Hi <name>, welcome! I’m <buddy>. When you’re ready, drop a message here and I’ll help with any access issues. No need to meet unless you want — I’ll lurk and reply. Link to starter doc: <confluence link>."

Manager async onboarding summary template (short doc header):
- Role: 
- Success signals by week 2: (1) PR merged with reviews, (2) passes local tests, (3) one cross-team intro completed.
- Known constraints: infra creds pending / hardware delay / license.

Unresolved questions / risks to track in hiring notes:
- Does the team need a dedicated training sprint to cover internal tools (k8s overlays, internal auth)?
- Are there legacy repos that still require SSH keys and manual provisioning? If yes, log in linked_artifacts.

Backfill protocol (if hire is replacing an immediate vacancy):
- Snapshot the outgoing owner's top-5 priorities and current work-in-progress.
- Create a 1-page triage doc for the incoming IC with explicit runbook pointers.
- If critical pager shifts exist, keep a 48-hour overlap with outgoing engineer if possible.

Signals of success (by day 10):
- New hire can independently run core dev/test flow locally.
- At least one small PR merged and reviewed.
- Buddy and manager report candidate has momentum and reasonable independence.

Quick templates & artifacts (copy/paste):
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — quiet-launch info + day 0 checklist"
- Welcome email body: 3 bullets + links + buddy intro + calendar stub.

Notes to self / triage items (open):
- Add a short checklist for security training completion that is less than 20 minutes.
- Consider a micro-credential badge for "silent-launch-ready" buddies.
- Track average time-to-first-PR metric for different teams; start collecting after next hire.

References / links:
- Onboarding runbook (internal): CONFLUENCE:IC-ONBOARD-2024 (see linked_artifacts).
- Hiring ticket template: JIRA-HIRE-9812.
- Starter code repo: github.com/redwood/starter-templates (link in linked_artifacts).

If you adopt this doc: please copy into the team onboarding folder and rename to include the team name (e.g., "platform-first-10-days-quiet-launch"). Keep this purposely informal — intent is to reduce noise, not bureaucracy.

Last edits: Aisha P. — trimmed synchronous items; added day-10 handoff packet; flagged training TODOs.

Unstructured brainstorm fragments:
- Could we have a single Slack channel #onboard-quiet for blockers only?
- Tiny stipend for coworking coffee in week 1 to nudge async questions into a backlog?
- Measure differences in eng ramp where buddy is same-level vs senior-level buddy.

End.
